There’s plenty of discussion about how AI could take some of our jobs, but what about the field of stand-up comedy?
 
Comedian Garrett Millerick has created G-Dog 2.0, using over a decade of his own comedy material. He performed alongside his AI double during the Festival Fringe in Edinburgh.
 
Reporter Ammie Sekhon meets Garrett to learn about the technology he used for this AI comedy partner, which reacts to the audience in realtime.

author: BBC News
description:
The US and Denmark have announced a deal on Greenland's security, resolving a diplomatic dispute sparked by President Donald Trump's threats to seize the territory by force.
 
The announcement comes after months of threats by Trump to "take" Greenland over national security concerns.
 
Trump said the agreement would grant the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs" in the semi-autonomous Danish territory.
 
The leaders of Denmark and Greenland welcomed the deal to "strengthen security" in the region.

description:
Nine bodies of murdered women have been found in Johannesburg in similar circumstances since July.
 
Most of the victims were young, in their 20s or 30s, and almost all had suffered extreme violence before their deaths.
 
Women in the city have taken to the streets to march against the violence, after previous protests in South Africa over the high rates of femicide.

author: BBC News
description:
We speak to a US/China tech expert who served under presidents Biden and Trump about America’s race with China to develop Artificial Intelligence. Does he agree with president Trump’s statement “whoever wins AI wins”, and what does “winning” look like?

Justin, Marianna and Anthony discuss Donald Trump’s rejection of any regulation for Artificial Intelligence, and whether this is in line with public opinion in the United States.

The team also talk about Congress, and how Republicans are reacting to Donald Trump’s most outspoken comments yet on AI. Plus, could Democrats be making the issue more central to their campaigning ahead of this November’s midterm elections? It’s an issue which has also united progressive Democrat senator Bernie Sanders and former Trump adviser Steve Bannon - what was their message to voters?

Our guest this week is Chris McGuire, a US-China technology expert with the Council on Foreign Relations. He’s a former senior advisor at the State Department for Trump
title: US v China - who’s ahead in the race to develop AI? | BBC Americast

author: BBC News
description:
Police in Spain's North African territory of Ceuta used batons and fired rubber bullets into the air to control crowds, as they moved hundreds of migrants from beaches to a tent camp. Tens of thousands of migrants crossed from neighbouring Morocco to Ceuta in July. At least 100 people died in the attempt. Though most of the migrants went back, several thousand have remained in the Spanish territory.
